claim: The table teaches 月, 火, 木, 土 and 本 as words with one reading each, but they stay silent character cards from earlier units, against the rule that a kanji the book also teaches as a word is one voiced word card.
evidence: Book: "月(つき) moon", "火(ひ) fire", "木(き) tree", "土(つち) soil", "本(ほん) book". Cards: chapter-5 r-d9b59879f3b8 月 "Moon; month" (getsu, gatsu / tsuki), r-efb2620838c4 火 "Fire", r-8294db3a2006 木 "Tree", r-d3cc0cab9c63 本 "Book; basis", chapter-4 r-90fbc9b1ac2e 土 "Soil", all with no reading or audio. Reading scheme: "A single kanji the book also teaches as a word in its own right ... is ONE item: the word, with its reading, and it has audio."
fix: Turn each into a word card with the book's reading (つき, ひ, き, つち, ほん) and audio, or confirm that a character card already carded stays as it is.
verdictReason: Verified in cards.json: chapter-5 月, 火, 木, 本 and chapter-4 土 carry no ttsText and no audio (pronunciation lines 'getsu, gatsu / tsuki' etc.), while this chapter's table reader produced each as kind 'word' with the book's reading (agent-logs/01-readingTableReader.json) and as-generated.json still has them voiced (ttsText つき, ひ, き, つち, ほん). The book pass then handed the book's meaning to the earlier generated character card and dropped the chapter's word card as a repeat (docs/designs/reading-decks/10-character-cards.md), so the word sense the scheme requires ('a single kanji the book also teaches as a word is ONE item: the word, with its reading, and it has audio', src/reading/readingSchemes.js) was lost. 水, 上, 下, 中 and 人 show the intended outcome: their earlier cards were word cards (みず, うえ, した, なか, ひと) with audio. Severity raised to should-fix: five common words (本 'book' among them) have no voiced reading card anywhere in the deck, and the cause is in the book pass, so every later R&W chapter whose table turns a generated kanji into a word will repeat it. Fix is the first option (turn each into the word card, same id so the delivered card updates in place), and the book-pass code is where to fix it.
